title: Daily Brain #002: the $96 shirt
notes: Checked by hand: the sale price is 80% of the original, so original = 80 / 0.8 = 100. Check: 100 − 20% = 80.
The wrong answer: adding 20% back to $80 gives 80 × 1.2 = 96, because 20% of the sale price ($16) is smaller than 20% of the original ($20).

The claim is labelled 'A common answer', not an AI and not a statistic: it is the usual trap of percentage problems. To run this as 'Beat the AI', paste a real logged model answer and fill claim.source (the validator requires it).

scenes.title: Spot the mistake
scenes.question: A shirt costs *$80* after a *20% discount*. What was the original price?
scenes.narration: A shirt costs eighty dollars after a twenty percent discount. Someone says the original price was ninety-six. Right or wrong?
Wrong. Eighty dollars is eighty percent of the original price. Eighty divided by zero point eight is one hundred. Adding twenty percent of eighty only adds sixteen.
